paper_summary: Al 7075 matrix syntactic foams with 2-4 mm hollow bubble alumina spheres (Alodur KKW) were made by a recyclable gravity-assisted pressure infiltration casting (720 C, 0.1 MPa). Six cylindrical foams (density 1.72-1.78 g/cm3, filler 60-63 vol%, total porosity 43-46%) were compression tested at 1 mm/min per ISO 13314; three were T6 aged. T6 raised 1% proof strength (up to 71.2 MPa), plateau stress (up to 60.9 MPa) and energy absorption (up to 27.8 MJ/m3) but shifted failure from ductile to brittle; densification strain 0.49-0.56.

extraction_notes: strength_mpa = compressive 1% proof strength per ISO 13314 (Table 5). Plateau stress = mean stress between 20-40% strain. Energy absorption W taken as reported (MJ/m3). Strain rate converted from 1 mm/min crosshead and 30 mm sample height (5.6e-4 1/s). Filler volume fraction and total porosity converted from %. Total porosity is the foam's total void fraction from hollow sphere interiors (Eq. 3), NOT matrix porosity, so stored in microstructure_notes. Particle mean diameter left null (only 2-4 mm range given); supplier bulk density 0.5-0.75 g/cm3 is a bulk, not true, density so left null. Elastic modulus not reported. Energy efficiency (0.73-0.91) has no schema field. Test temperature assumed room temperature.
